text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High-severity - GPU OOM + container restarts on node gpu-pool-13 (service: runtime-infer). Auto-page to oncall.
oncall-ryan: taking it. oncall responding, joining bridge in 2.
sre-lee: seeing a restart loop on pod runtime-infer-5467, restarted 3x in last 8m. Kernel logs show driver reset.
ml-runtime: paste of recent container logs:
```
2026-03-16T21:14:03Z ERROR runtime: CUDA error: out of memory
2026-03-16T21:14:03Z WARN kernel: GPU kernel reset detected (rc=116)
2026-03-16T21:14:04Z INFO prefill: prefill_length=180k tokens, model=redwood-7b-v1, kv_cache_alloc=43GB
2026-03-16T21:14:05Z INFO container: terminating pid=2345, exit=137
```
ml-runtime: root cause likely a huge prefill from a single customer session, memory allocation spiked and triggered kernel reset -> container restart.
oncall-ryan: any external 5xx or customer-facing errors? metrics show 502 spikes for one tenant.
ops-bot: telemetry: tenant=atlas-ai, requests impacted=18, pct_5xx=12%, avg-latency-up=2.1x during window.
cs-jordan: cc @oncall-ryan - Atlas reported "generation failed" 20m ago, will proactively notify once we have mitigation.
infra-maya: I'm isolating node gpu-pool-13 from scheduler (cordon + drain) to stop noisy restarts. running:
```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-pool-13
kubectl drain node/gpu-pool-13 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
sre-lee: mitigation plan (short):
- apply per-tenant prefill cap (max_prefill_tokens=16384) at routing layer
- enable small-context fallback model (redwood-7b-compact) for Atlas
- add kvcache eviction threshold and aggressive trimming for long sessions
- temporarily scale up dedicated pool + add conservative admission-control
oncall-ryan: can we do the routing change without deploy? we have dynamic routing policies.
ml-runtime: yes — pushing policy change now: routing rule:
```
{
  "tenant": "atlas-ai",
  "prefill_limit": 16384,
  "fallback_model": "redwood-7b-compact",
  "enforce_on_connect": true
}
```
ops-bot: policy applied, ack=success, change_id=policy-20260316-01 :white_check_mark:
sre-lee: also toggled kv trim to aggressive on affected model group:
`kv_cache.max_age_seconds=30` and `kv_cache.eviction_target=0.25`
infra-maya: node drained, restarting affected pods onto healthy nodes. observed one failed restart on new node due to CUDA driver timeout -> manual restart fixed it.
oncall-ryan: customer impact summary for CS/PM: Atlas saw ~18 failed requests, degradation window ~15m. No data loss, only transient failures. We will message them.
cs-jordan: suggested customer message draft:
"We're investigating transient failures affecting some long-context generations. We've applied temporary limits and a fallback model to restore service while we investigate a root cause. No data was lost. Expect reduced max context for affected sessions."
pm-ana: SLA-wise — is this going to be an ongoing risk? what about other tenants running long-prepills?
sre-lee: short answer: risk exists for any tenant with >50k token prefill. Longer-term: need prefill admission control + better kvcache accounting + model memory-aware scheduler.
ml-runtime: suspected memory accounting bug: allocations during prefill were not charging temporary spikes to the session cap -> we'll open bug with allocation trace attached.
oncall-ryan: action items:
- SRE: collect kernel traces + gpu dmesg (lee) — assigned
- ML runtime: repro harness for long prefill and memory accounting (ml-runtime) — assigned
- Infra: node health sweep and driver sanity check (infra-maya) — assigned
- CS: send customer note to Atlas + monitor (cs-jordan) — assigned
- Create incident ticket and postmortem (oncall-ryan) — assigned
sre-lee: quick commands i ran for traces:
```
# get dmesg around kernel reset
journalctl -k -u nvidia-driver -S "2026-03-16 21:10:00" -U "2026-03-16 21:20:00"
# collect GPU stack trace
nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,used_memory --format=csv
```
ml-runtime: temporary hotspot mitigation: set `max_prefill_bytes=35GB` and `prefill_streaming=trim` for the model group. Will monitor.
oncall-ryan: marking incident as mitigated for live traffic. moving to postmortem cadence. please add notes to the incident thread.
cs-jordan: sending message to Atlas now. will ping in-thread when done.
cs-jordan: message sent to Atlas support with reference INC-20260316-01 :envelope_with_arrow:
ops-bot: incident update: severity -> high, status -> mitigated, incident_id -> INC-20260316-01
pm-ana: thanks team. follow-up: prioritize prefill admission-control and memory-accounting fixes in next sprint.
oncall-ryan: closing live pager. if we see new restarts, I'll reopen. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: please attach logs and kernel traces to the incident ticket before EOD.
sre-lee: adding initial notes and will follow up with kernel traces + allocation flame.
